newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia bows to opposition and halts insurance sale.
newsitem.headline: Russia bows to opposition and halts insurance sale.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Alfred Kokh suspended the planned privatisation of Russia's biggest insurer OAO Rosgosstrakh in response to strong opposition to the sale, Kokh's spokeswoman said on Friday.
On Thursday night Kokh signed a regulation stopping Rosgosstrakh's privatisation. Russia's lower parliament State Duma is bitterly oppsed to it.
"Kokh signed the regulation to show that he is unbiased and in response to an unprecedented campaign against the Rosgosstrakh privatisation," spokeswoman Viktoriya Vergelskaya told Reuters.
Under the Rosgosstrakh privatisation scheme, employees bought 20 percent of shares and a management team has a priority right for a further 30 percent.
The remaining 50 percent were to be sold at an auction this year at 500 roubles per share with a face value of two roubles.
Vergelskaya said the official reason for the halt was a report from the Audit Chamber, which found legal violations in the project.
The Duma, which considers the price of Rossgosstrakh sale too low, asked the independent chamber to look into the company's privatisation plan.

But Vergelskaya said Kokh considered the Rosgosstrakh privatisation scheme legally correct. She said the Justice Ministry and the Federation Council's constitutional committee supported Kokh's point of view.

After the Duma appealed to President Boris Yeltsin to cancel Rosgosstrakh's privatisation in April, Kokh suggested suspending the sale until a special law on Rosgosstrakh privatisation was passed to the Duma by the government.
The draft law was to be sent to the Duma by July 1, but so far has not been sent.
Vergelskaya quoted Kokh as saying that Rosgosstrakh would be able to prove the legality of the privatisation scheme in court.
Rosgosstrakh chairman Vladislav Reznik said he planned to file a suit against the State Property Committee.
"Employees, those who have bought the shares, will force me to do this," he said. "I am absolutely sure we shall win."
